Zambia Technology Services Sector Faces Disruption Amid Influenza Outbreak

LUSAKA — Zambia’s Technology Services industry is contending with operational challenges after an outbreak of a severe influenza strain swept through multiple workforce clusters in Lusaka and Copperbelt provinces. The outbreak, which began last week, has already led to the temporary closure of several technology parks and data service centers.

According to the Zambia Technology Services Association, over 1,000 workers from major firms such as Kwacha Digital Solutions and ZamTech Innovations have reported flu-like symptoms, with approximately 40% of affected staff requiring medical leave. “We are currently operating at reduced capacity, with some teams working remotely where possible,” said Mwila Chanda, spokesperson for ZamTech Innovations. “The health and safety of our employees remain our top priority, but ongoing projects have experienced delays.”

Analysts estimate that output across the sector has dropped by 30% since the outbreak began, impacting software development, IT support, and cloud services. “The shortage of on-site technical staff has interrupted project timelines and forced several companies to defer client deliverables,” noted Mumba Mulenga, a Lusaka-based industry consultant.

Industry trade groups have called for urgent government assistance to help firms manage the situation and ensure continuity plans are robust. “We urge all members to follow enhanced hygiene protocols and provide flexible work arrangements,” said the Zambia Technology Services Association in a statement.

As of today, authorities and company officials continue to monitor the situation, but there is no clear timeline for when full staffing and operations across affected sites will resume.
